problemStatement.plain: AVAILABLE: Can the unique factorization be proved in a way that avoids the parent file, giving a self-contained proof of the Fundamental Theorem from Mathlib primitives?.

knowledge.progressSummary: PROGRESS: FTA proved via Finsupp approach. 12 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms. Key result: finsupp_prime_prod_factorization (factorization of Finsupp prime power product = original Finsupp), plus uniqueness and existence FTA. Docker build pending.
builtItems: factorization_finset_prod: helper lemma (∏ m ∈ s, m).factorization = ∑ m ∈ s, m.factorization
fta_support_prime: elements of factorization support are prime
fta_mem_support_iff_dvd: p ∈ support ↔ p ∣ n (for prime p)
fta_uniqueness: g.prod(·^·) = n with prime support → g = n.factorization
fundamental_theorem_of_arithmetic: ∃! f with prime support and f.prod(·^·) = n
factorization_determines_number: injectivity of factorization on positive naturals
factorization_eq_iff_valuations: m = n ↔ ∀ p, m.factorization p = n.factorization p
insights: Nat.factorization and Finsupp.prod (·^·) are mutual inverses on prime-supported Finsupps
factorization_finset_prod (distribution over products) proved by induction using Nat.factorization_mul
For prime p: (p^k).factorization a = if p = a then k else 0 — key for indicator-sum uniqueness argument
finsupp_prime_prod_factorization is the algebraic core: (f.prod (·^·)).factorization = f for prime-support f
The Finsupp FTA (∃! f with prime support and f.prod(·^·) = n) has the canonical witness n.factorization
